id: title:eli-r-ph:add the fold repair verb and pair for ambiguous groups

review.posthog_relevance: Adds a `--pair` CLI argument and associated parsing, execution, and recovery-reporting support to the person identity repair workflow, enabling operations/support to specify an old UUID and a new UUID for folding or merging ambiguous identities. This supports PostHog's person identity consistency recovery and divergence recovery workflows.

observations.behavior: Adds a new command-line argument --pair to the person_consistency repair command, allowing users to specify an old UUID and a new UUID for folding or merging ambiguous person identities.
observations.posthog_connection: This command is used by PostHog operations or support to repair person identity consistency, specifically folding a lost person into a survivor or merging two live persons. The argument allows specifying the pair of UUIDs to repair.

observations.behavior: Passes the new pair option to the repair execution, including it in the options dictionary.
observations.posthog_connection: This connects the command-line argument to the repair execution, allowing the fold or merge operation to use the specified pair of UUIDs.

observations.behavior: Updates the module docstring to clarify that the repair verbs can now fold a lost person into the person that holds its distinct ids, not just restore a lost person or merge two live persons.

observations.posthog_connection: This clarifies the purpose of the repair verbs, indicating that they can now handle folding a lost person into a survivor, not just restoring or merging.

observations.behavior: Adds the string "folded" to the set of recognized verbs in the report file.
observations.posthog_connection: Allows the divergence recovery workflow to recognize the "fold" verb alongside existing verbs like "merged" and "already_restored".

observations.behavior: Adds a "pairs" parameter to load_rows and its callers, and updates the docstring and row-filtering logic.
observations.posthog_connection: Supports specifying a mapping of an old person UUID to a live survivor UUID, which the recovery scan uses to resolve ambiguous identity mappings.
